prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1316; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Driver 1 was stopped in traffic on a Houston roadway when the vehicle behind, operated by Driver 2, struck the rear of Driver 1's car. Driver 1 reported pain in the left knee and was accompanied by a Passenger at the time of impact. Officers confirmed that both occupants were present in the vehicle at the scene, and the Passenger's presence is supported by statements taken at the location. Driver 1 is listed as the named driver on the insurance policy for the damaged vehicle.

The damage to the rear bumper, trunk lid, and tail lamp assembly of Driver 1's car is consistent with the impact described by both drivers. Photographs taken at the scene confirm several of the reported details, including the final resting positions of the vehicles. A few older scratches are visible on the rear panel, and it is not certain whether these predate this collision. No independent witnesses were located, so the account rests on the statements of the parties and the physical evidence.

It is not yet clear whether the knee injury reported by Driver 1 resulted from this crash. Medical records have not been reviewed, and the matter remains open pending further information.
